locator.text: Display 118.2, p. 118, in the proof of Proposition 10.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean fixes the radii absolutely instead of choosing them: r_0 = z_0 = 1/4 (supportCylinder is r² ≤ 1/16, |z| ≤ 1/4), and the plateau on which the cutoff is 1 is r² < 1/32, |z| < 1/8 — the axial plateau is exactly z_0/2 but the radial plateau r < 1/(4√2) ≈ 0.177 is larger than the paper's r_0/2 = 1/8, so the Lean plateau is not the paper's. The support statement is the weaker tsupport ⊆ the closed cylinder rather than compact containment ⋐ in the open one. Most importantly the paper's choice is constrained: it picks τ_0, z_0 with C_0(τ_0 + z_0^{1/D}) < q_*/2 so that by (10.3) the support of c lies in q < q_*/2, inside the local domain Ω_* = {τ > 0, q < q_*}; no such constraint, and no occurrence of q_* or of (10.3), appears in SpatialLocalization.lean. Smoothness in (r², z), the bounds 0 ≤ χ_x ≤ 1 and axisymmetry (spatialCutoff_rotation) do match. Rated low rather than medium because the margin the paper's constraint buys is not needed in the Lean development: the Lean local fields are built on PhysicalWaveSum.preterminal = {w | w.1 < 1}, i.e. they are defined and smooth on the whole time slab t < 1 rather than only on Ω_*, so an arbitrary fixed cylinder is admissible, and Proposition 10.1's conclusions are in fact proved (PaperLocalization.local_theorem_with_compact_candidate).
